title: performance(canary): auto-detect latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Aisha Patel
description: Adds automated performance-canary detection and rollout guard logic to the serving stack. Motivation: repeated incidents where subtle latency regressions in kernel selection and batching config propagated to production because there was no automated detection tied to rollouts. This PR implements (1) a lightweight real-time detector service that ingests aggregated latency and throughput metrics from canary traffic, (2) adaptive thresholds with hysteresis based on baseline distributions to avoid noisy flips, (3) KV-cache-aware signal adjustments for tail latency on long-context workloads, and (4) rollout guard integration that pauses/rolls back canary traffic and notifies on-call when thresholds are breached. The feature is behind the feature-flag perf_canary_auto_detect and is enabled by default only in staged and canary rings. Included in this change: new detector microservice (go), a controller hook in the rollout manager to call detectors and actuate pause/rollback, updates to the canary orchestration logic to support automatic hold/retry/backoff, dashboards and alerts (Grafana + Alertmanager rules) for newly computed signals, unit+integration+perf tests (simulated canary traffic harness), migration notes, and a rollout checklist. Checklist: - [x] detector implementation and core algorithm - [x] controller integration and API contract - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] simulated perf canary scenarios and regression tests - [x] docs (runbook + console widgets) - [x] feature-flag gating and default off for prod global. Important notes: detector uses EWMA+quantile summaries to track baseline and recent windows; thresholds are adaptive but capped to prevent over-permissive behavior; KV-aware adjustments add a per-model multiplier derived from profiling histograms. Rollout plan: enable on staging for 48h, roll to canary ring 5% for 24h, monitor signals and then 25%/75%/100% every 6h if stable. Linear and SUP links attached. This PR intentionally avoids making changes to model-serving kernels; it only observes metrics and actuates rollout decisions. Post-merge actions: run migration job to create detector config namespace (scripts/migrations/create_detector_config.sql) and update alertmanager routing to include ops-team. See docs/runbooks/perf-canary.md for operator instructions.

review_comments: Marco Li (reviewer): The overall design looks good. Two concerns: 1) Can we avoid any blocking call path in the controller? If the detector endpoint is slow it could affect control plane latency.

Aisha Patel (author reply): Thanks Marco. Detector calls are non-blocking by default; controller will call Evaluate with a 200ms timeout and falls back to conservative hold on timeout. I've added controller-side circuit breaker (see rollout_controller.go). For region config: detector configs are namespace-scoped and replicated via the migration job; we're adding a consistency check in the controller that logs if a model's detector config is missing.
Sofia Gomez (reviewer): Can the detection algorithm produce false positives during load spikes? We should surface a human-readable reason in the UI when a canary is paused/rolled back.

Aisha Patel (author reply): Good point. Detector now returns a structured reason string (algorithm, metric, value, threshold) and the rollout UI shows it in the canary status pane. Also added hysteresis windows to reduce transient false positives.
Ethan Wang (reviewer): Confirmed unit tests and perf tests. One nit: add telemetry counters for detector invocation latency and failure reasons.
Aisha Patel (author reply): Added metrics perf_detector.invocations, perf_detector.latency_ms and perf_detector.errors with tagged reasons.
QA (comment): Ran simulated canary with injected 12% latency regression and KV-heavy workload; detector triggered pause and rollback as expected. Logs attached in CI artifacts.
Ops (comment): Alertmanager rules look OK, but please include runbook link in the alert payload. Added in follow-up commit.
Marco Li (approved): Approving after addressing non-blocking and telemetry nits.
merge_commit: f1e2d3c4: squash merge perf-canary auto-detect + rollout guards
release_notes: Automated performance canary detection and rollout guards: adds detector service, controller integration, KV-aware hysteresis, dashboards, and runbook. Feature gated behind perf_canary_auto_detect. Operators must run migration scripts to create detector config namespace.
notes_for_operators: After merge: 1) run scripts/migrations/create_detector_config.sql in each region's control plane DB; 2) ensure feature flag perf_canary_auto_detect is off in global prod unless enabling for staged/canary rings; 3) verify Alertmanager routing to ops-team before enabling; 4) refer to docs/runbooks/perf-canary.md for incident handling.
estimated_risks: Medium: automated rollbacks could cause churn if thresholds are miscalibrated; mitigated by feature flag, hysteresis windows, and staged rollout. Additional risk: detector service availability; mitigated by controller circuit-breaker and conservative hold behavior.
notes_for_reviewers: Key files to review: services/perf-detector/* for algorithm correctness, controllers/rollout/rollout_controller.go for non-blocking integration and backoff, observability rules for alert fidelity. Pay attention to thresholds and KV multipliers.
